default._resident_note_1096: **#1096 the terrain-layer toggle (epic #1068, EL10c): 462,368 → 462,376 B (+8).** Measured on both board profiles, which link identically, and reproduced by CI's `embedded` job at the same figure on both — this baseline is the fix for the guard failure that run reported, not a pre-emptive bump. The board's whole share of EL10c is **one `bool`**: `obc_render::MapRenderer` gains `suppress_terrain`, the sticky per-renderer flag `MapRenderer::set_terrain_layer` writes and the collect pass reads when it builds the frame's visible-style mask, so a style carrying the terrain-layer flag (OBCM §2 style-record bit 5, #1095) is left out of the mask and its features are never decoded. Itemized exactly, and the cost is padding rather than the byte: `renderer` (`size_of::<MapRenderer>()`) 92,320 → 92,324 — every other field is a `heapless::Vec` of `(i32, i32)` / `Point` / `usize` / `f32`, so the struct's alignment is 4 and a 1-byte field costs 4 — and `app` (`size_of::<App>()`) 136,552 → 136,560, where `App`'s own alignment of 8 rounds that 4 up to 8. `App` is the resident static, so +8 accounted is exactly +8 linked, with no `.L_MergedGlobals` repacking in between. **No new statics, no new buffer, no frame growth**: nothing is allocated, the flag is one read per frame inside `collect`, `.data` stays 5,112 B, `.uninit` stays 1,024 B, and the guarded poll frame stays 9,728 B. The feature only ever *frees* per-frame scratch — a suppressed feature reserves no span, point or ring. **Provisional: this is a loan, not a floor.** The toggle exists so the #1097 ride review can A/B contours on one ride and is expected to be removed with that review's verdict (#1096); when it goes, these 8 B come back and this profile should return to 462,368.
default._resident_note_1072: **#1072 the set manifest's terrain role (epic #1068, EL4): 462,360 → 462,368 B (+8).** Measured on both board profiles, which link identically, and reproduced by CI at the same figure. The board's whole share of EL4 is one field: `sd::OpenSet` gains `terrain_bytes: Option<u32>`, the `Bytes` of the mounted set's manifest `terrain` record (`OBCA_Spec.md` §5.2), kept from the mount so `Storage::open_terrain` never re-parses the manifest — and so a `MS<id>.OBD` the manifest does *not* name is recognised as an orphan of a replaced set (§5.4) instead of being mounted, which would draw a rider a profile from the map they replaced. The hash-insensitive writable-symbol diff has exactly two real movers and they over-account by the usual linker padding: `__embassy_main::POOL` 33,064 → 33,072 (+8), the `Storage` living in main's async frame (which allocates every local at entry), and `SHARED_STORE` 6,536 → 6,540 (+4), the session copy. The eight `.L_MergedGlobals.*` groups that move sum to **zero** — pure repacking of the merged small-statics blocks — so +12 accounted lands as +8 linked. **No new statics and no new buffer**: the terrain slot, its extent table and its tile cache are all EL7's, already resident; this only remembers a length. `.data` stays 5,112 B, `.uninit` stays 1,024 B, and the guarded poll frame stays 9,728 B — the check is an integer comparison inside `open_terrain`, which is already `#[inline(never)]` and runs once at boot. Local flash 1,321,752 → 1,321,824 B (+72) on this host; `measured_flash` below is a CI figure and is re-pinned from this PR's `embedded` run.

default._boot_chain_note_1108: **Boot-path stack gates, added after the #1108 STKOF (schema v2).** Every image built from develop between #1084 (EL7) and #1108 hard-faulted at boot — a stack overflow at `link::init_store`'s prologue — and NOTHING in CI went red. The gap: `poll_frame_limit` only measures `TaskStorage<F>::poll` symbols, but the embassy **main task's** frame is allocated in the out-of-line `____embassy_main_task_inner_function::{{closure}}`, which that match excludes. EL7 inlined a ~2 KB terrain-parse temporary into it (20,352 -> 22,400 B) completely unseen. Three gates now cover it. `task_frame_limit` and `residual_stack_min` are EXACT measurements. `boot_chain_ceiling` is a deliberately CONSERVATIVE over-approximation: the walk follows every direct `bl` edge whether or not the path is feasible (a `Mode::ReadOnly` `open_file_in_dir` monomorphization still references `alloc_cluster`/`update_fat`, so FAT-write frames a rescan can never execute are counted) and is blind to indirect calls, so it is a drift detector, NOT a stack-safety proof — the on-glass high-water in ARCHITECTURE_RESOURCE_BASELINE.md is that. `boot_chain_headroom_min` is the invariant tying the other two together: ceiling and residual are independently re-approvable numbers, and #1084 failed precisely because three individually-reasonable changes summed past the stack, so the combination needs its own gate. Validated against the bricked image: on 5de00ce the same code reports task frame 22,400 B and headroom -7,932 B (chain 56,532 vs residual 48,600), versus 20,352 B and +7,044 B on the fix.

ble._resident_note_1072: **#1072 the set manifest's terrain role (epic #1068, EL4): 462,360 → 462,368 B (+8).** Measured on both board profiles, which link identically, and reproduced by CI at the same figure. The board's whole share of EL4 is one field: `sd::OpenSet` gains `terrain_bytes: Option<u32>`, the `Bytes` of the mounted set's manifest `terrain` record (`OBCA_Spec.md` §5.2), kept from the mount so `Storage::open_terrain` never re-parses the manifest — and so a `MS<id>.OBD` the manifest does *not* name is recognised as an orphan of a replaced set (§5.4) instead of being mounted, which would draw a rider a profile from the map they replaced. The hash-insensitive writable-symbol diff has exactly two real movers and they over-account by the usual linker padding: `__embassy_main::POOL` 33,064 → 33,072 (+8), the `Storage` living in main's async frame (which allocates every local at entry), and `SHARED_STORE` 6,536 → 6,540 (+4), the session copy. The eight `.L_MergedGlobals.*` groups that move sum to **zero** — pure repacking of the merged small-statics blocks — so +12 accounted lands as +8 linked. **No new statics and no new buffer**: the terrain slot, its extent table and its tile cache are all EL7's, already resident; this only remembers a length. `.data` stays 5,112 B, `.uninit` stays 1,024 B, and the guarded poll frame stays 9,728 B — the check is an integer comparison inside `open_terrain`, which is already `#[inline(never)]` and runs once at boot. Local flash 1,321,752 → 1,321,824 B (+72) on this host; `measured_flash` below is a CI figure and is re-pinned from this PR's `embedded` run.
ble._resident_note_1076: **#1076 map-referenced altimeter (epic #1068, EL8): 462,312 → 462,360 B (+48).** Measured on both board profiles, which link identically. The whole increase is `App` growing 136,504 → 136,552 B — the single compile-time allocation entry that moved — and it is two additions, both plain scalars with no buffer behind them: `Activity`'s `AltitudeFusion` (+36 B: the `Option<f32>` offset, the EMA weight / accepted / gated counters, the consecutive-outlier run's mean and length, the re-seed tally, and the `Option<f32>` terrain reference) and `RideEngine`'s `pending_terrain: Option<(i32, i32)>` (+12 B, the one-shot that makes the terrain read happen at the fix cadence rather than per frame). **No new statics**: the sampler is the `TERRAIN` slot EL7 already placed, borrowed through the ride loop's existing `&'static mut`, so nothing here allocates a tile buffer or a cache. `.data` stays 5,112 B, `.uninit` stays 1,024 B, and the guarded poll frame stays 9,728 B — `sample_terrain` is a shallow call taking one `&mut dyn` and returning a `bool`, run sequentially between (never beneath) the render and plan paths. ble._resident_note_1075: **#1075 emit-time elevation fill (epic #1068, EL7): 458,736 → 462,312 B (+3,576).** Re-measured on the merge of #1073 (OBCM v12) into this branch: the same +3,576 either side of that merge, since neither change touches the other's allocations. Measured on both board profiles, which link identically. The hash-insensitive writable-symbol diff has exactly six movers and they account for 3,572 of the 3,576 (the remainder is linker padding): `TERRAIN` +2,152 — the new `.bss` slot holding an `obc_elevation::TerrainElevation` (a 32-byte OBCT header + source ref + the N = 4 tile cache, i.e. four 512 B tiles and their keys); `sd::TERRAIN_EXTENTS` +1,292 and `sd::TERRAIN_SOURCE` +8 — the terrain sidecar's own resident 64-run extent table and direct-read source, which cannot share the map/set `EXTENT_SLOTS` union because terrain is a *second* file open beside the map for the session; `NAV_PLANNER` 15,728 → 15,784 (+56) — the planner's `EleFill` (a `DeadBand<f64>`, the carried height, the raw min/max and the seen flag), which is emit state that must survive across steps; `__embassy_main::POOL` +48 and `SHARED_STORE` +12 — `sd::Storage`'s `open_terrain` handle field, in main's async frame (which allocates every local at entry) and in the session copy; and `obc_elevation::reader::GEN` +4, the parse-generation counter that lets a `TileCache` reject a stale mount. `.data` stays 5,112 B, `.uninit` stays 1,024 B, and the guarded poll frame stays 9,728 B — the fill deliberately adds **no** frame: the sampler and its cache are statics, and the per-segment densification runs in an `#[inline(never)]` helper below the emit-hop frame (#419/#501). Two new compile-time allocation entries name the block (`terrain` 2,152, `terrain_extents` 1,300) and `nav_planner` moves with the symbol. The whole block is resident whether or not a card carries a `.OBD` sidecar, on purpose: it is what keeps the sampler out of the plan frames, and a budget that moved with the card's contents would not be a budget. Local flash is +6,384 B on both profiles (1,313,452 → 1,319,836 on this host); `measured_flash` below is the last CI figure plus that delta and must be re-pinned from this PR's `embedded` run.

ble._resident_note: **Fix round (review of #1040): resident unmoved at 440,984 B, flash +7,328 B.** Nine findings' worth of correctness work and not one resident byte: `sd::Storage::open_upload` gained an owner tag (`Option<RawFile>` → `Option<(RawFile, UploadOwner)>`, so a BLE teardown can no longer close the handle the cable is streaming a set into), the cross-transport one-transfer gate became `obc_app::TransferGate` (an `AtomicU8` holding *which wire* claimed it, where an `AtomicBool` let a phone dropping off the radio release a gate the cable held), and the boot sweep swapped two bounded `heapless::Vec`s of directory entries for two 125-byte id bitmaps. All three land inside existing padding or replace something the same size — `.bss` 435,840 B and `.data` 5,144 B are byte-identical to the pre-fix tree, `.uninit` is unmoved at 1,024 B, the poll frame is unmoved at 9,728 B, and all 23 `compile_time_allocations` entries match without a single change. Flash is the only mover, and it is now a **measurement rather than a projection**: the `embedded` job (run 30610810321) links **1,236,752 B** on both the `default` and `ble` legs — 1,218,184 → 1,236,752, +18,568 B for the whole PR, of which the fix round is +7,328 as measured on the pinned host (1,259,944 → 1,267,272 at `default`; local hosts link a different absolute figure, which is why flash is not gated for board profiles and why the number below is CI's). The fix round's share is the enforcement itself — the `NotFound` arm in `delete_set`, the torn/short magic verdicts, the id-space and free-space announce refusals, the abort path into the set session, the allocator's directory walk, and the sweep's two-pass bitmap scan. Previously: 440,960 → 440,984 B (+24) for the volume-set receive path (#1039, epic #1016 P3b). A set is `1..=32` shards plus a manifest, so unlike every other object type its correctness lives *between* transfers and the device must remember what it has: `ObjectStore` gains `set_upload: Option<obc_app::SetUpload>`, which is a set id `u16`, a shard count `u8` and a 32-bit committed bitmap — 8 B plus the `Option` discriminant at align 4. Itemized by symbol diff against the identical tree at the merge base, and the four movers account for the 24 B exactly: `link::STORE` 13,528 → 13,540 (+12 — that field, in the one resident `ObjectStore`); `usb::data_plane::TRANSFER_ARM` and `ble::state::TRANSFER_ARM` 32 → 36 each (+8 total — the `Signal<Armed>` handoff, because `Armed` gained `SetShard(TransferControl, Receiver, SetPart)`, its widest variant); and the merged small-statics group `.L_MergedGlobals` 108 → 112 (+4, padding after that shift — the seven renumbered `.L_MergedGlobals.*` groups sum to 776 B on both sides). Nothing else moved: no new `.bss` buffer, and the manifest work deliberately owns none — `Storage::validate_committed_manifest` puts its 1,864 B `MAX_MANIFEST_LEN` buffer on an `#[inline(never)]` frame that is gone before the commit write, and `sweep_aborted_sets` is a boot-time frame, so the ~36 KB stack rule is respected rather than paid for in residency. `compile_time_allocations` moves in the two entries that are the same 12 B seen twice: `ble_object_store` 13,528 → 13,540 and its `ble_total` 37,570 → 37,582. Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B; `.uninit` unmoved at 1,024 B; the `default` and `ble` legs link the identical 440,984 B on the pinned host. **Flash is a projection, not a measurement**: it is not gated for board profiles and CI is the authority, so `measured_flash` below is the previous CI figure plus this change's locally-measured delta (+13,208 B: 1,246,736 → 1,259,944 on the pinned host at the `default` profile) and must be re-pinned from this PR's `embedded` run. Previously: 439,040 → 440,960 B (+1,920) for the volume-set FAT handle budget (#1026, epic #1016 P3b). `OBCA_Spec.md` §5 makes one logical map 1..32 physical files, and the epic's device-cost review requires a mounted set to hold **every** shard's handle open for the mount lifetime — re-opening per query would put a FAT directory walk in the render loop. `sd::SD_MAX_FILES` therefore goes 6 → 16: the 8 handles a DACH-shaped set needs (core + coarse + ~6 geometry) plus the unchanged 5-handle mid-ride peak documented above `SdSpi`, plus margin. The ceiling that leaves is stated rather than implied: `sd::SD_SET_MAX_SHARDS` = `SD_MAX_FILES − SD_RIDE_PEAK_FILES` = **11 shards**, against `OBCA_Spec.md` §5.2's cap of 32 — a larger set is refused at mount with `obc_reader::MountError::Handles(11)`, naming this device's cap, instead of failing an open mid-ride. **The whole increase is that one constant, and it costs 3× what the array does.** The fork's `FileInfo` (`filesystem/files.rs`) is `RawFile` 4 · `RawVolume` 4 · `current_cluster` 8 · `current_offset` 4 · `Mode` 1 · `DirEntry` 40 · `dirty` 1 = 64 B at align 4 on thumbv8m, held in `VolumeManager`'s `heapless::Vec<FileInfo, SD_MAX_FILES>`; ten more slots is 640 B per resident `VolumeManager`, and the image links **three**. Itemized by symbol diff against the identical tree with the constant back at 6: `__embassy_main::POOL` 31,312 → 32,592 (+1,280 — *two* copies of `Storage` inside main's async frame, because an async frame allocates every local at entry, the same #270 trap that put `MAP_EXTENTS` in its own `.bss` slot rather than inside `Storage`) and `SHARED_STORE` 5,728 → 6,368 (+640 — the copy that actually lives for the session). Nothing else moved: the same tree with `SD_MAX_FILES = 6` links exactly 439,040 B, so the rest of #1026 — the `MapSummary` growth for sets, `set_identity`, `delete_set`, the `MapChoice::set` field — costs **zero** resident bytes. Re-measured after the review fix round (the `SetShards` split, the ladder/version/handle mount checks, the shard-reader nav/POI guards, the pure entry classifier and delete plan): the same tree with `SD_MAX_FILES = 6` still links exactly 439,040 B, so none of those cost resident bytes either, and the fix round's own headline — `obc_reader::MountedSet` going from 14,924 B by value to 20 B, with the 14,084 B shard table moved into a caller-placed `SetShards` — does not appear here at all, because nothing on the device mounts a set yet: it is a *stack/frame* cost this PR makes impossible to incur later, not a `.bss` one, and the compile-time allocation table is unchanged in all 23 entries. Poll frame unmoved at 9,728 B. Figures are **CI's** (the `embedded` job is the gate); this is a case where the pinned local host links the *identical* 440,960 B, and CI's `default` and `ble` legs agree byte for byte (run 30589233369: 440,960 B linked resident, flash 1,218,184 B on both legs), which is where `measured_flash` below comes from. ble._boot_chain_note_1108: **Boot-path stack gates, added after the #1108 STKOF (schema v2).** Every image built from develop between #1084 (EL7) and #1108 hard-faulted at boot — a stack overflow at `link::init_store`'s prologue — and NOTHING in CI went red. The gap: `poll_frame_limit` only measures `TaskStorage<F>::poll` symbols, but the embassy **main task's** frame is allocated in the out-of-line `____embassy_main_task_inner_function::{{closure}}`, which that match excludes. EL7 inlined a ~2 KB terrain-parse temporary into it (20,352 -> 22,400 B) completely unseen. Three gates now cover it. `task_frame_limit` and `residual_stack_min` are EXACT measurements. `boot_chain_ceiling` is a deliberately CONSERVATIVE over-approximation: the walk follows every direct `bl` edge whether or not the path is feasible (a `Mode::ReadOnly` `open_file_in_dir` monomorphization still references `alloc_cluster`/`update_fat`, so FAT-write frames a rescan can never execute are counted) and is blind to indirect calls, so it is a drift detector, NOT a stack-safety proof — the on-glass high-water in ARCHITECTURE_RESOURCE_BASELINE.md is that. `boot_chain_headroom_min` is the invariant tying the other two together: ceiling and residual are independently re-approvable numbers, and #1084 failed precisely because three individually-reasonable changes summed past the stack, so the combination needs its own gate. Validated against the bricked image: on 5de00ce the same code reports task frame 22,400 B and headroom -7,932 B (chain 56,532 vs residual 48,600), versus 20,352 B and +7,044 B on the fix.
